subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Archaeological site photography projects involve systematic photographic documentation of structures and artifacts.
• The Pompeii Project (scope: 350 photographs) was an Italian documentation effort completed in 2011.
• It recorded an ancient villa complex discovered during excavations at Pompeii.
• The Petra Archive (scope: 5,000 photographs) was a Jordanian documentation effort completed in 2018.
• It recorded the rock-cut temple facades at the archaeological site of Petra.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two projects. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: While The Pompeii Project recorded an ancient villa complex discovered during excavations at Pompeii, The Petra Archive recorded the rock-cut temple facades at the archaeological site of Petra.
choices.B: Compared to the 5,000-photograph Petra Archive, the archaeological photography project The Pompeii Project is relatively small in scope, at 350 photographs.
choices.C: Involving systematic photographic documentation of structures and artifacts, The Pompeii Project and The Petra Archive are both archaeological site photography projects.
choices.D: A prime example of an archaeological site photography project can be seen in The Pompeii Project, a 350-photograph Italian documentation effort recording an ancient villa complex discovered during excavations at Pompeii.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it most effectively emphasizes a similarity between the two projects. The sentence begins by identifying their shared methodology—'systematic photographic documentation of structures and artifacts'—before explicitly stating that both The Pompeii Project and The Petra Archive fall into the same category of 'archaeological site photography projects.' By leading with what the projects have in common and using the inclusive language 'both,' this choice directly accomplishes the goal of emphasizing similarity rather than highlighting differences in scope, location, or subject matter.
